html:
SMTO-FIL-0011 — SMTO couldn't use that file or folder location

GUID: f4669a06-3c84-4c8f-969b-788d90afa8a6
Slug: file-invalid-path
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The location SMTO used is blank, too long, contains characters the computer doesn't allow, or would copy or move a folder into itself. SMTO stopped at that step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Tell SMTO the full location of the file or folder exactly as it appears on that computer, for example /home/maria/reports/summary.txt or C:\Users\maria\reports. A complete, exact location leaves SMTO nothing to guess or shorten wrongly.
  2. If you asked to copy or move a folder, pick a destination outside that folder, and make sure the source and destination aren't the same place. Copying or moving a folder into or onto itself can't finish safely, so SMTO refuses it.
  3. Shorten very long file or folder names, and remove characters the computer doesn't allow in names, such as < > | ? * on Windows. Names that are too long or use characters the computer forbids are refused before anything is done.
  4. When copying between two Gateways, don't use .. (meaning "the folder above") in either location; give the full location instead. Copies between Gateways only accept locations that don't climb into a parent folder.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the file or folder and the copy, move or other action completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the location you meant, to the person who manages SMTO. If this happened partway through copying or moving a folder, look in the destination before asking again, because some items may already be there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation rejected a path operand that is empty, contains NUL, exceeds 4096 characters or the OS name rules, contains '..' in a Gateway-to-Gateway transfer path, or names a copy/move destination equal to or inside its own source.

What this means

  • A path is empty, malformed, oversized or OS-invalid, contains prohibited transfer parent traversal, or attempts a copy/move onto itself or inside its own source directory. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A path is empty, malformed, oversized or OS-invalid, contains prohibited transfer parent traversal, or attempts a copy/move onto itself or inside its own source directory.

How to diagnose it

  • Check target-native syntax and resolved source/destination identities, including hard links to the same file.

How to fix it

  • Inspect path_context and the message in the receipt. Supply a non-empty, OS-valid path under 4096 characters; for gateway.copy use paths without '..' components; for file.copy/file.move choose a destination that is neither the source nor inside a source directory (gateway_core/file_common.validate_path, file_manage.copy/move, transfer_paths.transfer_path).
  • Use platform-valid path syntax on the selected target.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Valid distinct operands pass the selected operation's path and containment checks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
